newsitem.title: USA: USWC prods prices fall with lower NYMEX market.
newsitem.headline: USWC prods prices fall with lower NYMEX market.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast products eased Monday, with traders getting little direction from New York refined products futures prices, which were nearly unchanged, traders said.

On the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), unleaded gasoline futures for August delivery itched up a mere 0.02 cents a gallon to 57.94 cents, while heating oil saw the same increase -- 0.02 cents -- to 52.78 cents.

Los Angeles CARB gasoline fell a half cent to 54.50/55.50 cents a gallon with San Francisco CARB one cent higher from Thursday to 55.50/56.50 cents, on perceived decreases in supply following several recent export cargoes, traders said.
Exports have resulted from weak profits at West Coast refineries, where the cost of raw material -- crude oil -- has greatly surpassed what refiners can fetch for refined products.
Traders said the cargoes of products were shipped to the Far East and southeast U.S markets.
Buyers of conventional grade gasoline, for sale in Reno, Nevada, offered to pay one cent less than Friday, or 53 cents a gallon, traders said.
Reformulated gasoline, for sale in the metropolitan Phoenix area, was talked one cent below CARB levels,traders said.
CARB diesel in Los Angeles fell around 1.50 cents a gallon to 55/56.50 cents.
